proofs.proof_tex:
Under Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}complete\text{-}randomization}\), the balanced count is \(n=N/K\), every arm has \(n_a=n\), and the counts exhaust the population:
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a=Kn=N,
\qquad n_{\mathrm u}=0.
\]
Thus the balanced allocation support \(\mathcal Z_{N,K}\) is precisely the specialization of \(\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\) with \(\mathbf n=n\mathbf 1_K\), and both laws are uniform on that same finite set.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\) therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}n\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N.
\]
Multiplication by \(C\) and \(C^{\mathsf T}\) yields the displayed formula for \(\Sigma_C(Y)\), and the scalar formula follows from the same lemma after substituting \(n_a=n\).  Finally, each diagonal \(S_{aa}(Y)\) depends only on the empirical marginal \(F_a\); hence only off-diagonal cross-arm covariances vary over \(\mathcal S_N(F)\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization with \(n_a\geq1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and unassigned count \(n_{\mathrm u}\geq0\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N},
\]
and therefore
\[
\Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}\right\}C^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\rho_W(Y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}
-\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\]
For fixed armwise empirical marginals \(F\), the diagonal terms are constant over \(\mathcal S_N(F)\), so all completion dependence is carried by the off-diagonal cross-arm covariances, with coefficients independent of \(\mathbf n\) and \(n_{\mathrm u}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(T_{ia}=\mathbf 1(Z_i=a)\) and \(p_a=n_a/N\).  Feasibility gives \(n_a\geq1\), \(\sum_a n_a\leq N\), and, since \(K\geq2\), \(N\geq2\); hence every denominator below is positive.  For the uniform law \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\) of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}sample\text{-}assign\text{-}design}\), counting allocations in \(\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\) gives
\[
\mathbb E_ZT_{ia}=p_a,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ja})=\frac{n_a(n_a-1)}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j),
\tag{1}
\]
and, when \(a\ne b\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ib})=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{jb})=\frac{n_an_b}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j).
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the first-order probability in (1) is the fraction \(n_a/N\) of positions carrying label \(a\); conditioning on one such position leaves \(n_a-1\) copies of that label among \(N-1\) positions.  For (2), after a position receives label \(a\), exactly \(n_b\) of the remaining \(N-1\) positions receive label \(b\).  This argument allows \(n_{\mathrm u}>0\), because the unassigned label is simply another fixed-count label.

Write \(y_i^a=Y_i(a)-\bar Y(a)\).  Then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i^a=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^N(y_i^a)^2=(N-1)S_{aa}(Y),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i^ay_i^b=(N-1)S_{ab}(Y).
\tag{3}
\]
The first identity in (1) first proves design unbiasedness:
\[
\mathbb E_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
=\frac1{n_a}\sum_{i=1}^N p_aY_i(a)=\bar Y(a).
\tag{4}
\]
For \(i\ne j\), (1) yields
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{ja})
=-\frac{p_a(1-p_a)}{N-1},
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_Z(T_{ia})=p_a(1-p_a).
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^a=-(\sum_i(y_i^a)^2)\), equations (3)--(5) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
&=\frac1{n_a^2}\left[
p_a(1-p_a)\sum_i(y_i^a)^2
-\frac{p_a(1-p_a)}{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^a
\right]\\
&=\frac{p_a(1-p_a)N}{n_a^2(N-1)}\sum_i(y_i^a)^2
=\left(\frac1{n_a}-\frac1N\right)S_{aa}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
For distinct arms, (2) gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{ib})=-p_ap_b,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{jb})=\frac{p_ap_b}{N-1}\quad(i\ne j).
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^b=-\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b\), equations (3), (4), and (7) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a),\widehat{\bar Y}(b)\mid Y\}
&=\frac1{n_an_b}\left[
-p_ap_b\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b
+\frac{p_ap_b}{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^b
\right]\\
&=-\frac{p_ap_bN}{n_an_b(N-1)}\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b
=-\frac1N S_{ab}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) proves
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(\widehat\tau=C\widehat{\bar Y}\), covariance equivariance gives the displayed formula for \(\Sigma_C(Y)\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}contrast\text{-}risk}\), cyclicity of trace, and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) then yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_W(Y)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[H\left\{
\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N
\right\}\right]\\
&=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}
-\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal S_N(F)\) fixes the multiset in each arm, hence fixes every \(S_{aa}(Y)\).  Equation (10) therefore proves the completion-dependence assertion.

For the smallest audit with an unassigned unit, take \(K=2\), \(N=3\), \(n_1=n_2=1\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=1\).  The support consists of all six ordered placements of the labels \(1,2,a_{\mathrm u}\).  Averaging over those six assignments makes each selected arm index uniform on \(\{1,2,3\}\), so (4) holds exactly.  Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
=\frac13\sum_i(y_i^a)^2=\frac23S_{aa}(Y),
\]
and the six ordered distinct-index pairs give
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(1),\widehat{\bar Y}(2)\mid Y\}
=\frac16\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^1y_j^2
=-\frac16\sum_i y_i^1y_i^2=-\frac13S_{12}(Y).
\]
These are exactly (6) and (8), so the optional-remainder boundary passes exhaustive finite enumeration.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the finite two-arm sample-and-assign design of Aronow, Green, and Lee, \(N\geq4\), \(n_{\mathrm s}\) units are sampled without replacement, \(m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) sampled units are treated, \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) are controls, and \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\) are unassigned.  For the difference-in-means estimator, their Equation (2) is
\[
V_N=\frac1{N-1}\left\{
\frac{N-m_{\mathrm t}}{m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{11}^{(N)}(Y)
+\frac{N-(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t})}{n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{00}^{(N)}(Y)
+2\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)
\right\}.
\]
Given the two finite-population marginal distributions, their Lemma 1 states sharp lower and upper bounds for \(\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)\), and the upper endpoint is attained by the comonotone coupling.  This is an oracle finite-population statement about known marginal distributions, distinct from their subsequent asymptotic analysis of estimated bounds.

source.verbatim_statement: The upper bound is attained if y1 and y0 are comonotonic.

proposed.name: Uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design
proposed.construction:
For a feasible count vector \(\mathbf n=(n_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\), let \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a\) and
\[
\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}
=\left\{z\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm u}^{N}:
\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=n_a\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A,
\quad
\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf 1(z_i=a_{\mathrm u})=n_{\mathrm u}
\right\}.
\]
The uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law is
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}(Z=z)
=\lvert\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\rvert^{-1}
\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal Z_{N,\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\}.
\]
The label \(a_{\mathrm u}\) records an unassigned unit and has no associated observed arm outcome.  For each assigned arm, the observed mean is
\[
\widehat{\bar Y}(a)=\frac{1}{n_a}\sum_{i:Z_i=a}Y_i(a).
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The generalized design requires an explicit support, probability law, unassigned label, and observed-mean map without altering the balanced allocation definition.

\[
\Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}\right\}C^{\mathsf T}
\]
and hence
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\]
Therefore all completion dependence is carried by the off-diagonal cross-arm covariances.

prose_updates.tldr: Under uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization with arbitrary positive arm counts and any nonnegative unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) exactly when \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. The off-diagonal completion objective and exact \(2/N\) regret identity do not depend on the arm counts. The result includes the full finite two-arm Aronow--Green--Lee oracle design, while balanced complete randomization remains an exact subdomain for the six-unit audits and the separate balanced-kernel copositivity theory. For admissible balanced covariance tensors, finite exact recognition remains available for exact real-algebraic inputs; polynomial-time recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee give the sharp two-arm oracle endpoint for a random sample assigned with fixed treated and control counts, while generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact multi-arm contrast-geometry boundary that is uniform over unequal positive arm counts and optional unsampled units. On the realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design, a sharper classification for joint covariance dominance, and, on the distinct balanced nonexchangeable domain, an exact cut-copositivity representation modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the unequal-count sample-and-assign covariance decomposition, proves that its completion-dependent term is count-free, and uses finite rearrangement plus isolated binary witnesses to obtain the graph-Laplacian equivalence, exact regret, and Loewner classification without balance or divisibility restrictions. It recovers the full finite Aronow--Green--Lee oracle design with the normalization \(S_{ab}=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}/(N-1)\), retains exact balanced six-unit audits, and keeps the general balanced-kernel copositivity theorem and its computational residual questions on their original subdomain.

sampling_model.design: The headline design is uniform over assignments with prespecified positive arm counts \(n_a\geq1\) and an optional unassigned count \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_a n_a\geq0\). Balanced complete randomization, with \(K\mid N\), \(n_a=N/K\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), is retained as an exact subdomain. The separate kernel problem continues to range only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), so no general-design and balanced-kernel domains are conflated.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling. An unassigned label records units omitted from the experimental sample without making the potential outcomes random.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object. Under the headline law it uniformly chooses disjoint arm samples of sizes \(n_a\), leaving \(n_{\mathrm u}\) units unassigned; under the separate nonexchangeable balanced analysis it follows the known admissible law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every reported arm has known positive probability \(n_a/N>0\). The unassigned probability \(n_{\mathrm u}/N\) may be zero, and no outcome mean is defined for the unassigned label.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The structural endpoint conditions on the full armwise empirical marginals \(F\) and is therefore an oracle finite-population completion result. Aronow, Green, and Lee's Equation (2) and Lemma 1 supply the exact two-arm oracle benchmark; their later asymptotic analysis of bounds estimated from observed marginal samples is not claimed here.

prose_updates.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee study a population of \(N\geq4\) fixed units, sample \(n\) without replacement, assign \(m\geq2\) to treatment and \(n-m\geq2\) to control, and leave \(N-n\) unsampled. Their Equation (2) is exactly the two-arm specialization of the fixed-count covariance identity after using \(S_{ab}=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}/(N-1)\), and their Lemma 1 supplies the sharp comonotone oracle endpoint. This finite known-marginal equivalence is distinct from their subsequent asymptotic theory for estimated bounds. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion for a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance algebra but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem agrees with the pairwise rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here is finite and direct. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The separate general-kernel theorem remains restricted to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a finite cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result is a sufficient identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem, not the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
prose_updates.interpretation: For any uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign experiment, a practitioner can ignore the unequal diagonal sampling coefficients when comparing potential-outcome completions: only the common term \(-N^{-1}\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}S_{ab}\) varies. Nonpositive off-diagonal entries of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\) certify one-sort least-favourable completion, while a positive entry identifies two arms on which a finite binary reversal strictly improves the loss. This conclusion is unchanged by unequal allocation or unsampled units. Matrix-valued conservativeness remains much rarer, and the nonexchangeable balanced-design analogue remains a finite copositivity problem rather than part of the generalized uniform design.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate is an oracle completion theorem for a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not estimate unknown armwise marginals and does not turn the endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. The full Aronow--Green--Lee finite design and sharp known-marginal endpoint are recovered, but their estimated-bound asymptotics are not reproved. For general nonexchangeable balanced kernels, the copositivity theorem is exhaustive rather than scalable: it enumerates factorially many relabellings and arm permutations and exponentially many supports, and strict witnesses may use as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The uniform fixed-count cone theorem follows from exact assignment-indicator moments, the count-free cross-arm covariance coefficient, a finite rearrangement proof, and a contrast-geometry necessity construction. Its domain permits arbitrary positive arm counts and a nonnegative unassigned remainder; balanced complete randomization is only a retained specialization. The two-arm statement recovers the Aronow--Green--Lee oracle variance formula and sharp comonotone endpoint, not their asymptotic estimated-bound results. The six-unit propositions remain balanced finite audits. The general balanced-kernel contribution remains the proved finite cut-copositivity equivalence and, for exact real-algebraic inputs, a terminating exact algorithm. No polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.
